WELCOME TO Dorset House School PART OF THE LANCING COLLEGE FAMILY OF SCHOOLS
Welcome
At Dorset House, we aim to provide a magical prep school experience for our pupils in an environment where children are engaged, enthused and inspired. We are often described as a greenhouse not a hot house and we find that pupils grow in confidence in our high challenge/low threat atmosphere.
Our committed and talented staff foster close links between home and school and we know every child well, meaning that we are aware of any successes achieved or issues they are facing.
Our optional flexi and weekly boarding for our Prep children, promote independence.
Happy, confident – not arrogant young people, who can relate to and communicate with others – Dorset House children often win awards and scholarships to senior schools and regularly going on to hold positions of responsibility.
Prospective parents often comment on the warmth of this school and if that is something which is important to your family, please call to make an appointment to visit us. We look forward to meeting you.

Parents’ Association
The Dorset House Parents’ Association is essentially a fundraising body. We organise events throughout the school year that we hope are inclusive, fun and add a social aspect to the school for parents to enjoy. The main focus of these activities is to raise as much money for the school as possible. We have, in the past, been able to provide a new Astro turf for the one of the courts, new sports equipment and new instruments for the Music Department.
In recent years, events have included a Party at the beginning of the Autumn Term; Bonfire Party for the whole school; Christmas Party; Christmas Market; Quiz Night; Summer Party and a Summer Ball.
Parents can also get involved with `DH Dads’ cricket or take part in charity events such as a 5K run on the South Downs.
Each year has a class representative who liaises with the committee and their class parents and acts as a line of communication from parent to school. This is most useful when there are new families in the school.
We work actively to include parents in the decision making as much as possible and have recently begun to survey the parents so that we can serve them in the best way possible whilst raising money for our chosen project that year. Each parent gives up their time to be on the committee and each member is extremely valuable to the success of the PA as a whole.

Bury Manor Pre-School
In September 2014, Dorset House invited Tracey Brooks, of Cootham Pre-School, to open a setting on our site and so Bury Manor Pre-School opened its doors to children aged 2 – 5 years. Children at the Pre-School enjoy complete access to the incredible grounds that Dorset House has to offer.
During its first Ofsted inspection, this setting received an `Outstanding’ rating and anyone who visits will be able to see why. The report states that the staff have excellent knowledge of how the children learn and develop and that they enjoy highly stimulating and challenging experiences. It goes on to say that the children’s behaviour is exemplary.
The Pre-School is situated in the Pre-Prep building in a new purpose-built room with its own outside space and, whilst independent of Dorset House School, the Pre-School works very closely with the Headmistress and all staff, enjoying a shared ethos.
An appointment to view the Pre-School can be made by calling Tracey Brooks on 07722 501416 or by emailing: burymanorpreschool@gmail.com.

Headmistress' Welcome
Welcome to Dorset House School
Welcome to Dorset House School, a community I am proud to lead as Headmistress, a school where children are truly at the heart of everything we do. At Dorset House, we aim to provide every pupil with the opportunity to thrive in a warm, nurturing environment and to learn through a rich and varied curriculum.
Forward thinking yet steeped in tradition, Dorset House is one of the oldest prep schools in the country catering for both day and boarding pupils. Founded in 1784 in Hertfordshire, before moving to Littlehampton, we now educate pupils aged 4–13 on a stunning 16-acre site within the South Downs National Park, in the quiet village of Bury overlooking the River Arun.
Our small, nurturing classes enable children to benefit from individualised teaching, with subject specialists from year 5 to year 8. Quoted as “positively championing childhood”, we celebrate what it means to be a child, whether exploring the woodlands and zen garden or taking part in a wide range of extra-curricular activities and enrichment opportunities.
Academic rigour and excellence are part of the school’s DNA, with pupils progressing to a wide range of senior schools such as Brighton College and Seaford College, as well as further afield to Bryanston or Stowe. Our merger with the Lancing College family of schools has created further collaborative opportunities across the curriculum, alongside a clear pathway to Lancing College for those for whom it is the right choice.
Our pupils are proud of their school. I love nothing more than visiting them in their classrooms, where they are eager to share their learning with anyone who comes in, and where the excellent relationships they enjoy with their teachers are evident. It was the pupils who sold me the school and I have no doubt they will do the same for you!
While the written word can give you a flavour of our ethos and values, I wholeheartedly recommend that you come and visit us to see for yourself what a special place Dorset House is. I look forward to meeting you and your children very soon.
With very best wishes,
Sarah Sutherland-Booth
Personal tours and open mornings can be booked by contacting the School Registrar, Sarah O’Brien (sobrien@dorsethouseschool.com).
The school is highly successful in meeting its aim to inspire children through a challenging approach to academic learning. Pupils consistently gain their first choice place in competitive entry to senior independent schools and each year a considerable number are awarded academic, music and sporting scholarships.

History of Dorset House
Under various names, Dorset House has been in existence since 1784, originally in Hertfordshire but for eighty years in Littlehampton. In 1964, the School, then in private ownership, closed there but during its last term, Bury Manor School charitable trust was set up by parents, old boys and friends of the School to purchase Bury Manor where Dorset House now resides. The trust still owns and runs the school via our Board of Governors. We are proud of the school’s long history and you will find the names of some of the ex-Headmasters in use as our four Houses are Wilkinson, Munro, Sims and Hutchinson and our Pre-Prep building is known as `Champs’ – named after Tony Champion (HM 1983 – 1988).
Bury Manor has an extraordinary history. In 1066 the records show it was then owned by Countess Goda, sister of Edward the Confessor, but the Normans handed it over to the Monks of Fecamp, a Benedictine monastic order who farmed the Manor for centuries. The Great Barn was built in the 16th Century.
It is interesting to note that in the past, Dorset House offered rowing, sailing and fishing. There was also the first Bury Scout Troop which involved both the children at DH and some local children from the village. Our new leadership programme echoes the activities enjoyed by children in this idyllic setting in the past.
Dorset House School joined the Lancing College family of schools in September 2025.

We know that many parents considering a move from London in particular, are looking for a traditional prep school in an idyllic country setting but with a forward thinking attitude. We believe that Dorset House ticks these boxes.
The school is on the banks of the River Arun in the heart of the South Downs National Park. The coast is just over 10 miles away.
There are many lovely Downland villages in the area and a wide variety of larger villages/small towns.

Prep Academic
Academic Life in the Prep School
At Dorset House, academic excellence is combined with care, encouragement and high expectations. Our Prep School provides a stimulating and supportive learning environment in which pupils are challenged to think independently, develop resilience and build a genuine love of learning.
We believe that children thrive when they are known well, taught well and supported with confidence and care. Small class sizes and dedicated subject specialists allow teaching to be tailored to individual needs, ensuring every pupil is supported to achieve their personal best.
A Broad and Ambitious Curriculum
The Prep School curriculum is broad, balanced and academically ambitious. Core subjects are taught with rigour and clarity, while a wide range of additional subjects enrich pupils’ learning and broaden their understanding of the world.
Lessons are designed to be engaging, purposeful and challenging, encouraging pupils to ask questions, think critically and apply their knowledge with confidence. Strong foundations in literacy, numeracy and study skills underpin progress across all areas of the curriculum.
Teaching That Inspires and Supports
Our experienced and passionate teachers foster positive, respectful relationships with pupils, creating classrooms where children feel confident to participate, make mistakes and learn from them. Teaching is carefully planned to meet the needs of different learners, with appropriate challenge and support built into every stage.
Regular assessment is used thoughtfully to inform teaching, track progress and ensure pupils are supported promptly where needed. Clear feedback helps pupils understand how to improve and take increasing responsibility for their learning.
Developing Independent and Confident Learners
As pupils move through the Prep School, increasing emphasis is placed on independence, organisation and perseverance. Children are encouraged to take ownership of their learning, develop effective study habits and build confidence in their abilities.
This approach ensures pupils are well prepared academically, socially and emotionally for the next stage of their education, whether progressing to competitive senior schools or tailored pathways that suit their individual strengths and ambitions.
Academic Excellence Within a Supportive Culture
Academic achievement at Dorset House is underpinned by strong pastoral care and a calm, focused learning environment. Pupils are encouraged to aim high while understanding that effort, curiosity and resilience are just as important as results.
The school’s most recent ISI inspection in 2026 recognised the strength of teaching, positive pupil attitudes to learning and the effectiveness of academic support throughout the Prep School.
Preparing for the Future
Dorset House Prep pupils leave with strong academic foundations, confidence in themselves and enthusiasm for learning. They are articulate, well‑rounded and well prepared for senior school life and beyond, ready to embrace challenge, seize opportunity and continue achieving with confidence.

Educated at Oxford, Aberystwyth and Cranfield Universities, John served in senior executive roles in the oil and gas and chemicals industries, but over the last two decades has increasingly focused on global risks, in particular climate change. Safeguarding
At Dorset House School, the safeguarding and welfare of our pupils is of paramount importance. We are committed to providing a safe, caring and supportive environment where children feel valued, listened to and protected from harm.
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. All members of staff, volunteers and governors share a collective duty to safeguard and promote the welfare of children in line with statutory guidance and best practice, including Keeping Children Safe in Education and Working Together to Safeguard Children.
Our Safeguarding Approach Dorset House School operates a robust Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy which is reviewed regularly to ensure it remains fully compliant with the latest statutory guidance, including:
Our policies and procedures clearly set out how safeguarding concerns are identified, recorded and responded to, including referrals to external agencies when necessary.
Staff Training and Responsibilities All staff are required to read and understand Part One of Keeping Children Safe in Education and undertake regular, up‑to‑date safeguarding and child protection training appropriate to their role. Training is refreshed at least annually and supplemented through ongoing safeguarding briefings and updates.
Designated safeguarding leaders receive enhanced training to enable them to fulfil their responsibilities effectively and to provide advice and support to colleagues.
Working with External Agencies Dorset House School works closely with external agencies, including children’s social care, health professionals, the police and local safeguarding partners, to ensure that pupils and families receive appropriate and timely support. We recognise the importance of effective information‑sharing and multi‑agency working in safeguarding children.

Pre-Prep
Welcome to Dorset House Pre-Prep. Our Pre-Prep is a place of laughter and excitement. We strive to inspire our pupils to develop a love of learning through teaching that is stimulating, creative and challenging. We make the most of our idyllic location, nestled in woodland and on the banks of the River Arun, through outdoor learning and Forest School. We have excellent teachers and support staff who work together to assess the children’s progress and development.
Dorset House prides itself on being one big family. The children in the Pre-Prep regularly spend their morning break times playing with older children in the woods. It is not uncommon to find football matches taking place where the players range in age from 5 to 13! The Pre-Prep mix together for various occasions throughout the year such as at Christmas and for Pre-Prep Science and Maths mornings. We have Pre-Prep assemblies once a week where we promote friendship, respect and tolerance of others.
In the Pre-Prep, children begin their learning through a variety of play-based activities in Reception, and gradually move on to more formal methods of teaching as they progress through Key Stage 1 and into Year 3. Our pupils enjoy bright, stimulating classrooms and have the opportunity to use the ICT suite, Science Lab, Music School and sports facilities that we share with the Prep school. Reception and Year 1 have direct access onto the outdoor learning area and we have a Forest School site within our school grounds.
“Children in the Pre‑Prep benefit from a nurturing and supportive environment in which they feel safe, valued and confident to learn.” — ISI Inspection Report, 2026.

About Us
Dorset House School is a vibrant and welcoming preparatory school set in the beautiful village of Bury, near Pulborough in West Sussex. As one of the oldest prep schools in the country (Founded in 1784), Dorset House enjoys a rich heritage and a reputation for developing confident, well-rounded children who love learning and embrace challenge.
Our unique rural setting provides an exceptional environment for childhood: open space, woodland, and historic buildings that together create a sense of freedom, creativity, and adventure. We nurture curiosity, individuality, and character through a balanced curriculum, outstanding pastoral care, and extensive opportunities for sport, music, art, outdoor learning, and leadership.
Dorset House recently joined the Lancing College family of schools, benefiting from the shared expertise, values, and educational vision of one of the region’s leading independent school groups. This partnership enhances our ability to offer an ambitious, enriching education while maintaining the warmth and close‑knit community that define Dorset House.
We believe deeply in kindness, integrity, and mutual respect. Our school is committed to providing a happy, inclusive, and aspirational environment where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to flourish.
